## 2016 Honda Civic Brake-Service Decision Snapshot
A 2016 Civic with 112,000 km and occasional brake squeal most often needs a brake-focused check first, then the least invasive fix that solves the noise and wear. With a **USD 900** budget, all three options fit financially, but they differ a lot in urgency and long-term value.

## Brake Options Decision Chart
| Option | Cost | Time | Urgency | Risk | Best Use |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| A) Front brake pads only | USD 240 | 1 day | Moderate | Low | Best if pads are worn and rotors are still smooth |
| B) Pads + rotors | USD 620 | 1–2 days | High | Medium | Best if rotors are grooved, warped, or causing repeat squeal |
| C) Full brake inspection + fluid change | USD 180 | Same day | High | Low | Best first step to confirm the real issue and refresh old fluid |

## Recommended Path for Your Budget
- **Best first move: C) Full brake inspection plus fluid change**
  - Lowest cost
  - Same-day turnaround
  - Helps confirm whether the squeal is from pads, rotors, calipers, or just brake dust
  - Brake fluid service is especially sensible at this mileage if it has not been done recently

- **Best repair if the issue is simple: A) Replace front brake pads only**
  - Good value if rotors are still in spec
  - Keeps total spend far below budget
  - Lower risk than replacing more parts than needed

- **Best repair if damage is beyond pads: B) Replace pads and rotors**
  - More complete fix
  - Better if squeal is paired with vibration, scoring, or uneven braking
  - Still comfortably within budget, but only worth it if inspection shows rotor wear

## Quick Decision Guide
- Choose **C first** if you want the safest, most cost-efficient diagnosis.
- Choose **A** if inspection shows rotors are healthy and the squeal is pad-related.
- Choose **B** if the rotors are worn, noisy, or uneven, or if you want the most thorough repair now.

## Sources
- Honda owner resources: https://owners.honda.com/
- Brake maintenance overview: https://www.brake.org/
- General vehicle service guidance: https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/maintenance/
